analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject. He causes תַּרְדֵּמָה (a deep sleep) to fall עַל הָאָדָם (upon the man). The next verb, וַיִּישָׁן (and he slept), confirms the effect on the man.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and assimilated root-initial נ.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּפֵּל, “caused to fall.” יַהְוֶה names the God who caused a deep sleep to fall on the man.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they form the subject of the singular verb וַיַּפֵּל, “he caused to fall.” The one who causes a deep sleep to fall on the man is therefore identified as YHWH God.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference and no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: תַּרְדֵּמָה is the direct object of וַיַּפֵּל. God caused a deep sleep to fall עַל הָאָדָם, “upon the man,” and וַיִּישָׁן, “and he slept,” confirms the result.
In וַיַּפֵּל … תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם, עַל introduces the man upon whom God caused a deep sleep to fall.
עַל הָאָדָם identifies the man upon whom God causes a deep sleep to fall. The singular verb וַיִּישָׁן (“he slept”) and the suffix in מִצַּלְעֹתָיו (“from his ribs”) refer to that same individual.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים causes a deep sleep (תַּרְדֵּמָה) to fall on the man (הָאָדָם). וַיִּישָׁן describes what the man then does: he falls asleep.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: The object אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו means “one of his ribs.” The next clause says that God closed up the flesh in its place, confirming that he removed the rib.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקַּח אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו means “he took one of his ribs.” אַחַת counts a single rib, agrees with צֵלָע in gender, and stands as the object of וַיִּקַּח.

אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו means “one of his ribs.” The suffix refers to הָאָדָם, the man. The feminine singular אַחַת selects one rib, and תַּחְתֶּנָּה refers back to it when God closes the flesh in its place.
analysis.morphology: Partitive מִן with נ assimilated to צ, followed by a plural construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix. Agreement is feminine here.

analysis.evidence: After taking one of the man's ribs, יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים remains the subject of וַיִּסְגֹּר. The following words בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה describe the flesh he closed up where the rib had been.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: After God takes one of the man's ribs, וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה says that he closed up the flesh in its place. בָּשָׂר names the tissue at the site of the removed rib.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular suffix refers to אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו, “one of his ribs.” After taking the rib, God closes up the flesh where the rib had been.
analysis.morphology: Preposition with a third-person feminine singular pronominal suffix.
